diagnostic_evidence.quote: Similar constructions can be carried out to obtain analogues of higher-order

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract asserts that the constructed non-linear formulae have the same accuracy as Newton-Cotes formulae on the same nodes, in general. The body only establishes this for two nodes (o(h^2), Lemma/Theorem) and three nodes (o(h^4), Theorem thm:construct). For more nodes the paper offers only the unproved remark that 'similar constructions can be carried out'; the three-node proof relies on the coincidence that a single condition (2alpha_1+alpha_2=0) kills both nonlinear error terms, and no argument is given that the count of nonlinear constraints stays within the number of free coefficients for higher node counts.

issues.overall_effect: The general-node accuracy claim in the abstract (and the 'similar constructions' remark) is unsupported; only the 2- and 3-node results are established.
issues.title: Abstract claims Newton-Cotes-level accuracy for arbitrary node sets; only 2- and 3-node cases are proved
issues.why_classification: The body is explicit about what is proved; restating the abstract's scope loses only an unproved generalization and no formal result changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: with $f(a)$ in the range of $f^*$ the equalities $q(\bar{f})=f(a)$

issues.failure_explanation: Exactness on lambda f^* (lambda in an interval around 1) forces q(y,y)=y and q^{(0,1)}(y,y)=1/2 only for y in {lambda f^*(a)}, not for all diagonal points as the proof asserts. Counterexample: f^*(x)=x+1, a=0, q(f_0,f_1)=(f_0+f_1)/2+psi(f_0) with psi smooth, psi=0 on (1/2,2), psi(10)=1. Then hat I is scalably exact on f^* (lambda in (1/2,2)), but for f≡10 the error is h, not o(h^2). The same gap affects lem:aff (its proof itself notes the restriction to the range of f^* but the statement still says all f in C^2), cor:pders (values of bar f unspecified), and thm:construct, where q_1 involves f^{*-1} and is undefined when f(a) lies outside R (e.g. f^*=e^x and f taking non-positive values), so the o(h^4) claim for all f in C^4(R) cannot hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to the statements the hypothesis that f(a) lies in {lambda f^*(a): lambda in (lambda_-,lambda_+)} (scalable case) or in the interior of the range R of f^* (affine case and thm:construct), and state the derivative identities in cor:pders at such diagonal points.
issues.overall_effect: The o(h^2) and o(h^4) guarantees of lem:noworse, lem:aff and thm:construct, and the derivative identities in cor:pders, are only valid for f with f(a) in the (scaled) range of f^*; for other f the statements are false or ill-defined.
issues.title: Scalable/affine exactness only constrains q on the diagonal within the target's value range, yet error bounds are claimed for all f
issues.why_classification: A hypothesis fix rescues method, rate and conclusions, but the advertised scope 'for all f in C^2/C^4' is genuinely reduced to functions whose values lie in the target family's range.

issues.failure_explanation: The value q^{(0,2)}(bar f^*) = -(1/6) f^{*''}(a)/[f^{*'}(a)]^2 is derived at the point (f^*(a),f^*(a)). The corollary then expands q around (f(a),f(a)) for a general f, which is only legitimate if f(a)=f^*(a). Applying exactness to lambda f^* instead gives q^{(0,2)}(lambda bar f^*) = -(1/6) f^{*''}(a)/(lambda [f^{*'}(a)]^2), so the coefficient depends on f(a). Check: for f^*=e^x the exponential rule (eq:qexp) expands as (f_0+f_1)/2 - (f_1-f_0)^2/(12 f_0), i.e. coefficient 1/f(a), whereas the corollary gives e^{-a}=1/f^*(a). Hence the stated formula is false whenever f(a)≠f^*(a), and the proposed 'improved trapezoidal rule' with fixed coefficient is not third-order exact on multiples lambda f^*, lambda≠1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add the hypothesis f(a)=f^*(a), or replace the coefficient by (f^*(a)/f(a)) f^{*''}(a)/[f^{*'}(a)]^2 (valid for f(a) in the scaled range), and adjust the remark accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary cor:added-1 and the following improved-trapezoidal-rule remark are incorrect unless f(a)=f^*(a); on other multiples of f^* the correction term has the wrong size.
issues.title: Curvature coefficient in Corollary is evaluated at f^*(a) but applied at f(a)
issues.why_classification: A short local correction of the coefficient, obtained by the same exactness argument, restores the full statement and the intended application.

Let $f^*:\Rset\to R\subseteq\Rset$ be bijective with inverse function

issues.failure_explanation: The step deducing q^{(0,1)}(y,y)=1/2 for every y in the range of f^* divides by alpha f^{*'}(alpha a+beta), which requires a preimage of y at which f^{*'}≠0; the hypothesis only gives f^{*'}(a)≠0. Counterexample: f^*(x)=x^3, a=1 (hypotheses satisfied). Affine exactness with alpha a+beta=0 forces q(0,epsilon)=epsilon/4, so q^{(0,1)}(0,0)=1/4, and for f(x)=x-1 the error is h^2/4, not o(h^2). The same target in thm:construct gives q_1(u^3,v^3)=(u+v)(u^2+v^2)/4, which is not C^1 at (0,0) and yields h q_2 ≈ 0.487 h^2 versus I=h^2/2 for f(x)=x-1, contradicting the o(h^4) claim; bijectivity does not guarantee the smoothness of q_1 that Corollary cor:pders and the expansion require.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume f^{*'}(x)≠0 for all x (f^* a smooth diffeomorphism onto R) in lem:aff, cor:pders and thm:construct.
issues.overall_effect: lem:aff, the affine part of cor:pders, and thm:construct are false for bijective targets with a critical point; the claims hold only when f^{*'} is nowhere zero.
issues.title: Affine-exactness lemma and construction theorem fail where f^{*'} vanishes
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard non-degeneracy hypothesis excludes only critical-point targets and preserves all conclusions and rates.

issues.failure_explanation: Linear independence of the polynomials p_j(xi)=xi^j-xi+1 (different degrees) does not imply independence of their evaluation vectors at the n-1 nodes; a nonzero combination of degree ≤ n could vanish at n-1 points. Invertibility actually follows from the special structure (xi_0=0 forces the constant and linear coefficients of any vanishing combination to be zero, and sum c_j=0 forces a root at 1, so p/xi^2 of degree ≤ n-2 has n-1 roots), an argument not given.

issues.failure_explanation: Matching the Taylor expansions at order h requires sum_k alpha_k = 1, an equation absent from the system j=2,...,n. The system therefore encodes exactness on x^1,...,x^n but not on constants, so 'exact on polynomials of order n-1' does not follow directly. It does hold indirectly (the Newton-Cotes rule with n odd satisfies all n equations and the system has a unique solution), but this reasoning is missing.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the observation that the Newton-Cotes rule (exact to degree n for odd n) solves the system and, by uniqueness, coincides with the solution, so sum alpha_k=1 holds automatically.

issues.failure_explanation: With f_1=f_0(1+eps), the first term expands as (f_0+f_1)/2 - f_0 eps^2/12 + O(eps^3) and the correction -(1/12)(f_0-f_1)log(f_0/f_1) = -f_0 eps^2/12 + O(eps^3). Their sum deviates from the two-point Gauss rule (f_0+f_1)/2 by -f_0 eps^2/6 = O(h^2), so h q has O(h^3) error, not o(h^4); e.g. on e^x the h^3 coefficient of the error is nonzero. With the sign +1/12 the eps^2 and eps^3 terms cancel and the rule is Gauss-Legendre plus O(h^4), giving the claimed o(h^4). As written, the claim is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the sign of the correction term to +(1/12)(f_0-f_1)log(f_0/f_1) (and fix f_1=f(a+(1-xi)h)).
issues.overall_effect: The concluding example of a 'non-linear Gaussian' o(h^4) formula is incorrect as displayed.
